newsitem.title: USA: Sony, Mariah Carey form record label.
newsitem.headline: Sony, Mariah Carey form record label.

text.p: Pop singer Mariah Carey has formed a joint-venture record label with Sony Corp., the company for which she has recorded six hit albums, the parties said on Wednesday.

Carey's label, Crave, aims to release six to eight albums a year, covering musical genres with "global appeal," a statement said. It will be headed by Rick Bisceglia, who was formerly senior vice-president at Arista Records, a unit of Bertelsmann AG.
"Our main goal is to have a close-knit label where artists can feel comfortable, where we can discover some great music and get it the attention it deserves," Carey said in a statement.
She continues to record for Sony-owned Columbia Records. Her latest album "Daydream" has sold just over 7 million copies in the United States since its October 1995 release, according to SoundScan.

The label's first signing is Allure, a female vocal pop group whose first single "Head Over Heels" was released several days ago. A spokesman said Crave is very close to signing one r&b group and two pop groups.
